jess-support: FYI a customer (BrightFrame) reports embeddings throughput dropped ~60% for their bulk /embeddings calls this morning. tokens/sec steady, vectors/sec tanking. API 200s but long tail latency. ticket #BF-8921. anyone seen this pattern? :thinking_face:
anna-ops: ugh. any client sample ID or request_id we can grep? also which model variant are they using?
jess-support: sent sample via DM. request_id: 2026-03-17T08:12:43Z-rq-7d3f. model: rf-embed-v2-quant. batch_size in their calls ~64.
mike-gpu: pulling infra metrics for that timeframe. initial glance: GPU util jumped to 98% on node pool gpux-dedicated-6 at 08:12, queue_depth for embed-workers spiked from ~10->120. looks like queue backlog.
lee-ml: rf-embed-v2-quant had a kernel tweak rolled 08:05 by canary rollout (kernel-selection optimization). could be interaction with batching. reopening rollout logs...
sre-bot: deploy-notification: rollout rf-embed-v2-quant kernel-tune v2026.03.17-0805 by mike-gpu. 3/3 canaries healthy.
anna-ops: can you paste the customer's small repro (curl) without keys? we need to repro locally if possible.
jess-support: paste: ```curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"rf-embed-v2-quant","inputs":["... repeated text ..."]}'``` they batch 64 per request, sending ~2k requests per minute.
mike-gpu: grabbing worker logs around rq-7d3f:
```
E 08:12:43 worker.cpp:246 batch_window=120ms, queued=118, processed=2
W 08:12:44 kvcache.cpp:92 miss_rate=0.31, lock_wait_ms=14
I 08:12:45 kernel_selector.cpp:184 using kernel hotpath=v3_packed
```
lee-ml: that batch_window=120ms is large. we default 40ms. did autosplit/batch-window config change?
anna-ops: I see a config push at 08:00 from infra: `embed_batch.window_ms = 120` for gpux pool as an attempt to improve cost. Possibly rolled into the same deploy.
mike-gpu: that explains queue_depth spike + full GPUs. larger window -> bigger batches -> higher per-batch memory and kernel stress for quant variant -> kernel hotpath hitting pathological path -> slow per-batch churn despite fewer calls.
jess-support: customer mentions SLO breaches and billing alerts; they're escalating to enterprise team. need ETA for mitigation.
lee-ml: quick mitigation options: 1) rollback batch_window to 40ms (config) 2) pin user to non-quant variant rf-embed-v2 (slower tokens but more predictable) 3) scale gpux pool by +25% (short term). I can patch a canary to reduce window to 40ms.
anna-ops: prefer config rollback so no model changes. mike, can infra revert embed_batch.window_ms on gpux-dedicated-6?
mike-gpu: doing rollback now. will push to canary then prod. triggering: `infractl config set embed_batch.window_ms=40 --pool=gpux-dedicated-6 && infractl rollout embed-batch-config --canary=2`
sre-bot: rollout-notification: starting canary embed-batch-config -> target gpux-dedicated-6.
(2m pass)
mike-gpu: canary looks good. queue depth on canary nodes dropped to ~8, GPU util down to ~60%. beginning global rollout.
jess-support: passed to customer; they report initial improvement on their side within 3 minutes. thanks team :+1:
lee-ml: follow-up: schedule postmortem to decide default batch_window for quantized variants and add a regression test that runs scaled batch load against kernel variants.
anna-ops: creating incident doc and escalation summary, will include repro steps, timelines, and config diff. adding BF-8921 notes.
jess-support: thanks all. I added customer note: temporary mitigation applied, enterprise team offered credits for SLO breach. will monitor for 2 hours. :eyes:
